quizQuestions.question: What is the primary role of the Enganche?
options: Linking midfield to attack with creative passing
quizQuestions.explanation: They act as the central hook, distributing balls to forwards.

carrilero.title: Carrilero
carrilero.description: A shuttle midfielder covering lateral spaces between lines.
carrilero.introduction: The Carrilero (shuttler) is a central midfielder who moves laterally. Instead of running box-to-box, they cover the wide spaces left open when fullbacks or playmakers push forward.

sections.heading: The Shuttler
sections.content: They play in a midfield three. Their primary job is defensive balance: they slide laterally to the left or right to secure wide areas when fullbacks overlap.

sections.heading: Positioning
sections.content: They rarely enter the opponent's box. They focus on maintaining possession and screening the wide channels.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary movement of a Carrilero?
options: Shuttling laterally to cover wide spaces
quizQuestions.explanation: A Carrilero moves sideways (laterally) to cover wide midfield gaps.

quizQuestions.question: Where is the Carrilero most useful?
options: In formations with attacking fullbacks (like diamond midfields)
quizQuestions.explanation: They cover the wings when fullbacks push high to attack.

quizQuestions.question: What is the English translation of Carrilero?
quizQuestions.explanation: Carrilero translates to shuttler or lane-player.

quizQuestions.question: Do Carrileros score many goals?
options: No, they focus on defensive cover and possession
quizQuestions.explanation: Their role is defensive balance and possession link-up, not scoring.

quizQuestions.question: How do they assist the defense?
options: By covering the wings when fullbacks overlap
quizQuestions.explanation: They slide wide to block counters down the flanks.

libero.title: Libero
libero.description: A sweeping defender with the freedom to carry the ball into midfield.
libero.introduction: The Libero (free defender) sits behind the defensive line. In possession, they have the freedom to carry the ball forward into midfield, acting as an extra playmaker.

sections.heading: The Free Man
sections.content: Defensively, they sweep up loose balls. In possession, they step out of defense and dribble into midfield, creating a numerical overload and starting attacks.

sections.heading: Modern Equivalent
sections.content: While rare as a central defender today, ball-playing center-backs (like John Stones) who push into midfield play a similar role.

quizQuestions.question: What does 'Libero' mean in Italian?
quizQuestions.explanation: Libero translates to free.

quizQuestions.question: What does the Libero do in possession?
options: Carries the ball forward into midfield to playmake
quizQuestions.explanation: The Libero is free to step out of defense and join the midfield buildup.

quizQuestions.question: Who is the greatest example of a Libero?
quizQuestions.explanation: Franz Beckenbauer perfected the Libero role, dominating from defense.

quizQuestions.question: Why is the traditional Libero rare today?
options: Flat defensive lines and offside traps are preferred
quizQuestions.explanation: A deep Libero would play opposing strikers onside, ruining modern offside traps.

quizQuestions.question: What modern player has played a role similar to the Libero?
quizQuestions.explanation: Stones has stepped out of defense into central midfield for Manchester City.

shadow-striker.title: Shadow Striker
shadow-striker.description: An attacking midfielder who bursts forward to score behind a target striker.
shadow-striker.introduction: A Shadow Striker operates behind a target striker. As the target man challenges defenders, the shadow striker bursts forward from midfield to score from loose balls or passes.

sections.heading: Attacking Mechanics
sections.content: They play as a No. 10 but focus on goalscoring. They wait for the target striker to win headers or hold up the ball, then sprint past them into the box to shoot.

sections.heading: Defensive Duties
sections.content: They must press the opponent's holding midfielder when defending, acting as a bridge.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary focus of a Shadow Striker?
options: Late runs into the box to score goals
quizQuestions.explanation: They act as goalscoring playmakers, arriving late in the box to finish chances.

quizQuestions.question: Who does the shadow striker play behind?
options: A target striker who holds up play
quizQuestions.explanation: They play behind a physical forward who creates space and knockdowns for them.

quizQuestions.question: What makes them hard to mark?
options: They start deep in midfield, making their runs late and unexpected
quizQuestions.explanation: Center-backs are busy with the striker, and midfielders fail to track their late runs.

quizQuestions.question: Which role is similar to the Shadow Striker?
quizQuestions.explanation: The second striker also plays off the shoulder of the main forward.

quizQuestions.question: Name a player known for this goalscoring playmaker style.
quizQuestions.explanation: Müller and Alli (at his peak) were famous for late, unmarked runs into the box.

raumdeuter.title: Raumdeuter
raumdeuter.description: A 'space interpreter' who exploits tiny holes in defenses from wide.
raumdeuter.introduction: The Raumdeuter (space interpreter) is a unique wide role. They do not dribble or cross; they use elite positioning and movement to appear in the box at the perfect second to score.

sections.heading: Finding the Gap
sections.content: The Raumdeuter drifts across the final third, looking for lapses in the opponent's defensive line. They 'ghost' into the box unmarked to tap in crosses.

sections.heading: Style
sections.content: They have average speed and dribbling but elite anticipation, making them highly effective goalscorers.

quizQuestions.question: What does the German word 'Raumdeuter' translate to?
quizQuestions.explanation: Raumdeuter means 'space interpreter' or 'space investigator'.

quizQuestions.question: Which player famously coined this term to describe himself?
quizQuestions.explanation: Thomas Müller coined the term to describe his unique positioning style.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary strength of a Raumdeuter?
options: Positional anticipation and finding empty spaces
quizQuestions.explanation: They rely on reading play to arrive unmarked in dangerous scoring zones.

quizQuestions.question: Where does a Raumdeuter typically start on the pitch?
quizQuestions.explanation: They start wide but constantly wander inside to find gaps.

quizQuestions.question: Do Raumdeuters focus on crosses and dribbles?
options: No, they focus on off-the-ball runs and tap-ins
quizQuestions.explanation: They prefer off-the-ball movement, arriving late to finish chances created by others.

box-midfield.title: Box Midfield
box-midfield.description: A central structure using four midfielders to dominate central play.
box-midfield.introduction: The Box Midfield uses four central midfielders (two holding, two attacking) to form a box. This shape provides passing triangles and central dominance.

sections.heading: Tactical Concept
sections.content: The box midfield completely overloads standard midfields (which use 3 players). It gives the team a 4v3 advantage, making central progression easy.

sections.heading: Width Sacrifice
sections.content: Because midfielders are central, the team relies on fullbacks to provide the attacking width.

quizQuestions.question: How many players form a Box Midfield?
quizQuestions.explanation: A box midfield utilizes four players (two deep, two advanced).

quizQuestions.question: What is an advantage of the box midfield?
options: It overloads the center, giving passing superiority
quizQuestions.explanation: Having four central players outnumbers standard three-man midfields.

quizQuestions.question: Who provides the width in a box midfield system?
quizQuestions.explanation: Fullbacks must push high and wide to provide attacking width.

quizQuestions.question: Which system uses a box midfield?
quizQuestions.explanation: Both the 3-2-4-1 and the 4-2-2-2 naturally form box midfields.

quizQuestions.question: What is a danger of the box midfield?
options: Lack of wing cover on counters
quizQuestions.explanation: If the fullbacks are high, the wide channels are vulnerable on turnovers.

wm-structure.title: WM Structure
wm-structure.description: The classic Herbert Chapman setup forming a W and an M shape.
wm-structure.introduction: The WM structure is a historic tactic forming a W (in attack) and an M (in defense). It revolutionized football in the 1920s by introducing a third defender.

sections.heading: Historical Context
sections.content: Invented by Arsenal manager Herbert Chapman in 1925 to counter the new offside rule. It changed the game from a 2-3-5 layout to a structured 3-2-2-3.

sections.heading: The W and M
sections.content: The defensive line (3) and holding mids (2) form the M. The attacking mids (2) and forward line (3) form the W.

quizQuestions.question: Who invented the WM structure?
quizQuestions.explanation: Herbert Chapman developed the WM at Arsenal in the 1920s.

quizQuestions.question: What numerical shape represents the WM?
quizQuestions.explanation: The WM is a 3-2-2-3 system (3 defenders, 2 holding mids, 2 attacking mids, 3 forwards).

quizQuestions.question: Why was the WM invented?
options: To counter the 1925 offside rule change
quizQuestions.explanation: The offside rule change made attacking easier, requiring a third defender to stay secure.

quizQuestions.question: Which part of the WM forms the 'M'?
quizQuestions.explanation: The three defenders and two holding midfielders form the M shape.

quizQuestions.question: What was the attacking shape of the WM?
options: A 'W' shape formed by attacking midfielders and forwards
quizQuestions.explanation: The two attacking midfielders and three forwards form the W shape.

pyramid-structure.title: Pyramid Structure
pyramid-structure.description: The historic 2-3-5 alignment that dominated early football.
pyramid-structure.introduction: The Pyramid (2-3-5) is the oldest tactical structure. It used two defenders, three midfielders, and five forwards, dominating football from the 1880s to the 1925 offside rule change.

sections.heading: Five Forwards
sections.content: Football was highly attacking in the Victorian era. The front five consisted of a left winger, inside left, center forward, inside right, and right winger.

sections.heading: Defensive Setup
sections.content: With only two fullbacks and three half-backs, defending relied on physical tackles and long clearances.

quizQuestions.question: What is the numerical setup of the Pyramid?
quizQuestions.explanation: The Pyramid is the classic 2-3-5 formation.

quizQuestions.question: When was the Pyramid structure dominant?
quizQuestions.explanation: It was the standard tactical baseline for early football.

quizQuestions.question: How many forwards were fielded in the Pyramid?
quizQuestions.explanation: The front line featured five forwards (the '5' in 2-3-5).

quizQuestions.question: Why was it called the 'Pyramid'?
options: The shape tapered from the 5 forwards down to the 2 defenders, forming an inverted pyramid
quizQuestions.explanation: The layout looks like an inverted pyramid (wide at the front, narrow at the back).

quizQuestions.question: What rule change ended the dominance of the 2-3-5?
options: Banning the goalkeeper from using hands
quizQuestions.explanation: The offside change forced teams to drop a midfielder into defense, leading to the WM.

michels-total-football.title: Rinus Michels' Total Football
michels-total-football.description: The space-centric Ajax and Dutch philosophy of fluid positional rotations.
michels-total-football.introduction: Rinus Michels developed 'Total Football' in the 1970s. The core idea was that players could swap positions fluidly during a match, creating space and confusing opponent marking.

sections.heading: Space Management
sections.content: Michels believed that space was the most important element. When attacking, you make the pitch as large as possible; when defending, you squeeze it.

sections.heading: Positional Interchange
sections.content: Outfield players had to be comfortable in defense, midfield, and attack, as they rotated constantly.

quizQuestions.question: Which coach is credited with inventing Total Football?
quizQuestions.explanation: Rinus Michels developed the system with Ajax and the Dutch national team.

quizQuestions.question: What is the key positional rule in Total Football?
options: Players can rotate fluidly if the shape is maintained
quizQuestions.explanation: Outfield players rotate positions dynamically, covering for teammates.

quizQuestions.question: What was Michels' focus regarding space?
options: Make the pitch large in attack, and compress it in defense
quizQuestions.explanation: Manipulating space was the core defensive and offensive tool.

quizQuestions.question: Which team reached the World Cup Final in 1974 using this style?
quizQuestions.explanation: The Dutch 'Clockwork Orange' side wowed the world in 1974.

quizQuestions.question: What does Total Football require from players?
quizQuestions.explanation: Since players swap, everyone must know how to defend and attack.

cruyff-positional-football.title: Johan Cruyff's Positional Football
cruyff-positional-football.description: Cruyff's style based on triangles, diamond midfields, and style.
cruyff-positional-football.introduction: Johan Cruyff modernized Total Football at Barcelona. He introduced the diamond midfield, focused on passing triangles, and believed that winning was nothing without style.

sections.heading: The Diamond Midfield
sections.content: Cruyff used a 3-4-3 diamond. This shape created passing triangles across the pitch, making it easy to retain possession.

sections.heading: Style over Results
sections.content: Cruyff famously stated: 'Winning is an important thing, but to have your own style, to have people copy you... that is the greatest gift.'

quizQuestions.question: What midfield shape did Cruyff favor in his 3-4-3?
quizQuestions.explanation: Cruyff's 3-4-3 used a diamond midfield to maximize passing lanes.

quizQuestions.question: Which club did Cruyff manage to create the 'Dream Team' in the 1990s?
quizQuestions.explanation: Cruyff led Barcelona's 'Dream Team' to their first European Cup in 1992.

quizQuestions.question: What was Cruyff's view on possession?
options: If you have the ball, the opponent cannot score
quizQuestions.explanation: Keeping the ball was both the main attacking and defensive strategy.

quizQuestions.question: What is a passing triangle?
options: Positioning players to always have two passing outlets
quizQuestions.explanation: Triangles ensure the ball carrier has two direct pass options.

quizQuestions.question: Cruyff believed that football should be...?
quizQuestions.explanation: Cruyff believed that football should be beautiful and entertaining for fans.

guardiola-juego-posicion.title: Pep Guardiola's Juego de Posición
guardiola-juego-posicion.description: Pep's rigid space structures that create free men on the pitch.
guardiola-juego-posicion.introduction: Pep Guardiola took Cruyff's ideas and created 'Juego de Posición'. It is a highly structured space-possession system designed to create the 'Free Man' through positional discipline.

sections.heading: Positional Discipline
sections.content: Players must hold their zones. If a winger drifts inside, the fullback must stay wide. This keeps the pitch stretched and creates passing options.

sections.heading: The 3-Second Rule
sections.content: Guardiola demands immediate counter-pressing within 3 seconds of losing the ball to stop counters at the source.

quizQuestions.question: What is the English translation of 'Juego de Posición'?
quizQuestions.explanation: Juego de Posición translates to Positional Play.

quizQuestions.question: What is Pep's view on player movement?
options: Players should roam anywhere they want
Players must stay in their designated zones to keep the shape
quizQuestions.explanation: Positional Play relies on strict discipline to maintain passing structures.

quizQuestions.question: Who is the 'Free Man' in Pep's system?
options: An unmarked player in space who can receive the ball
A player on a free transfer
quizQuestions.explanation: The system is designed to pass the ball until an opponent commits, leaving one player completely free.

quizQuestions.question: What is the 3-second rule?
options: Instant counter-pressing to win the ball within 3 seconds of losing it
quizQuestions.explanation: Pep's teams must press immediately upon turnover to recover the ball quickly.

quizQuestions.question: Which clubs has Pep Guardiola managed?
quizQuestions.explanation: Pep has had historic success at Barca, Bayern, and Man City.

klopp-gegenpressing.title: Jürgen Klopp's Gegenpressing
klopp-gegenpressing.description: Heavy-metal football focused on winning the ball in high transitions.
klopp-gegenpressing.introduction: Jürgen Klopp popularized Gegenpressing, describing it as 'Heavy Metal Football'. The team presses intensely the second possession is lost, using turnovers as their main playmaker.

sections.heading: The Playmaker Press
sections.content: Klopp believes that winning the ball back near the opponent's box is more effective than any playmaker, as the opponent is open and disorganized.

sections.heading: Intensity
sections.content: Demands incredible physical fitness. Players must sprint in groups to trap the ball carrier the second possession is lost.

quizQuestions.question: What term did Klopp use to describe his style?
quizQuestions.explanation: Klopp described his intense, fast-tempo style as Heavy Metal Football.

quizQuestions.question: What does Klopp consider the 'best playmaker'?
quizQuestions.explanation: Winning the ball high creates instant, dangerous chances without needing a playmaker.

quizQuestions.question: Which teams did Klopp lead to major finals using Gegenpressing?
quizQuestions.explanation: Klopp built historic Dortmund and Liverpool teams using this style.

quizQuestions.question: What is required from Klopp's players?
options: Exceptional stamina, sprint speed, and workrate
quizQuestions.explanation: High-intensity pressing requires elite physical fitness.

quizQuestions.question: How does Klopp's press react when the ball is won?
options: They attack forward at maximum speed
quizQuestions.explanation: The team exploits the transition, charging forward immediately to score.

mourinho-pragmatism.title: José Mourinho's Pragmatic Counter-Attacking
mourinho-pragmatism.description: Defending deep, denying spaces, and using counter-attacks.
mourinho-pragmatism.introduction: José Mourinho is the master of tactical pragmatism. He focuses on defensive organization, invites opponent pressure, closes all spaces, and strikes on lethal counters.

sections.heading: Pragmatic Focus
sections.content: Mourinho believes that the team that makes fewer mistakes wins. He is comfortable giving up possession, sitting in a low block, and waiting for the opponent to make a mistake.

sections.heading: Transition Lethality
sections.content: His teams are trained to transition from defense to attack in 3-4 passes, utilizing fast wingers and clinical strikers.

quizQuestions.question: What is the core of Mourinho's philosophy?
options: Tactical pragmatism, defensive stability, and counter-attacks
quizQuestions.explanation: Mourinho focuses on winning through defensive organization and minimizing mistakes.

quizQuestions.question: What is Mourinho's view on ball possession?
options: The team with the ball is more likely to make a mistake
Only keepers should have the ball
quizQuestions.explanation: Mourinho believes keeping the ball increases the risk of making an error in transition.

quizQuestions.question: Which team did Mourinho lead to a treble in 2010?
quizQuestions.explanation: Mourinho won the treble with Inter Milan in 2010, beating Barca and Bayern.

quizQuestions.question: What defensive block is most associated with Mourinho?
quizQuestions.explanation: Mourinho is famous for his organized, compact low blocks.

quizQuestions.question: How do Mourinho's teams play on transition?
options: Fast, direct vertical passes to attackers
quizQuestions.explanation: His teams break with speed, striking before the opponent can track back.

ancelotti-flexibility.title: Carlo Ancelotti's Flexible System
ancelotti-flexibility.description: Adapting system to fits players' qualities to keep them happy.
ancelotti-flexibility.introduction: Carlo Ancelotti is famous for his tactical flexibility and man-management. Instead of forcing players into a rigid system, he adapts his formation to suit his squad's strengths.

sections.heading: The Quiet Leader
sections.content: Ancelotti's 'quiet leadership' focuses on player relationships. He believes happy players perform best, so he tailors systems to keep his stars in their favorite roles.

sections.heading: Hybrid Formations
sections.content: His teams often defend in one shape (e.g. 4-4-2) and attack in another (e.g. 4-3-3) to balance the squad.

quizQuestions.question: What is Carlo Ancelotti's main tactical identity?
options: Adaptability and tailoring systems to fit his players
quizQuestions.explanation: Ancelotti is famous for being flexible, adapting his systems to match player strengths.

quizQuestions.question: What managerial quality is Ancelotti most famous for?
quizQuestions.explanation: Ancelotti is beloved by players for his calm, supportive man-management.

quizQuestions.question: Ancelotti is the first manager to win which trophy five times?
quizQuestions.explanation: Ancelotti has won a record five Champions League titles (with Milan and Real Madrid).

quizQuestions.question: What is a 'hybrid formation' Ancelotti uses?
options: Playing with a goalie in midfield
Defending in a 4-4-2 but attacking in a 4-3-3
quizQuestions.explanation: He often uses different shapes for defensive and offensive phases to maximize player output.

quizQuestions.question: How does Ancelotti handle star players?
options: Frees them to express their qualities within a balanced structure
Forces them to play defense only
quizQuestions.explanation: He adapts the team structure to allow star players creative freedom.

bielsa-man-pressing.title: Marcelo Bielsa's Man-Oriented Pressing
bielsa-man-pressing.description: Marcelo Bielsa's high-intensity system of tracking runners.
bielsa-man-pressing.introduction: Marcelo Bielsa (El Loco) is a tactical purist. He uses a high-intensity, man-oriented pressing system where defenders track their assigned runners across the entire pitch.

sections.heading: Man-to-Man Marking
sections.content: Bielsa's teams defend 1v1 across the pitch. Every player marks their opponent tightly, tracking them even if they swap sides.

sections.heading: Vertical Attack
sections.content: In possession, Bielsa demands rapid, vertical passing and constant off-the-ball sprints to overwhelm the defense.

quizQuestions.question: What nickname is Marcelo Bielsa known by?
quizQuestions.explanation: Bielsa is affectionately known as 'El Loco' due to his obsessive tactical focus.

quizQuestions.question: What is the core defensive method of Bielsa's teams?
options: Intense, man-to-man pressing across the entire pitch
quizQuestions.explanation: Bielsa's teams track opponents 1v1 all over the pitch.

quizQuestions.question: What is a main requirement for Bielsa's players?
quizQuestions.explanation: Strict man-to-man pressing requires elite stamina and running output.

quizQuestions.question: How do Bielsa's teams progress the ball?
options: Rapid, vertical passing and off-the-ball sprints
quizQuestions.explanation: His teams attack with speed and high player rotation.

quizQuestions.question: What is a risk of Bielsa's strict man-marking?
options: Defenders get pulled out of shape, leaving huge gaps if beaten
quizQuestions.explanation: If an opponent beats their marker, the entire defensive structure is compromised.

sacchi-zonal-pressing.title: Arrigo Sacchi's Zonal Pressing
sacchi-zonal-pressing.description: The AC Milan system of high-line defensive zones and press.
sacchi-zonal-pressing.introduction: Arrigo Sacchi revolutionized football in the late 1980s with AC Milan. He discarded man-marking, introducing a highly coordinated zonal pressing system with a compact high line.

sections.heading: Compactness
sections.content: Sacchi demanded that the distance between defense and attack be no more than 25 meters. This compressed the pitch, leaving opponents no room to play.

sections.heading: Moving as One
sections.content: The team moved relative to the ball, teammates, space, and opponents. Defenders moved in sync, catching strikers offside easily.

quizQuestions.question: Which legendary club team did Arrigo Sacchi manage in the late 1980s?
quizQuestions.explanation: Sacchi led AC Milan to back-to-back European Cups in 1989 and 1990.

quizQuestions.question: What defensive system did Sacchi replace man-marking with?
options: Coordinated zonal marking and high press
quizQuestions.explanation: Sacchi introduced zonal marking, where players cover spaces rather than tracking individuals.

quizQuestions.question: What was Sacchi's rule regarding team compactness?
options: Distance between defense and forwards should be under 25 meters
Spread players across the entire pitch
quizQuestions.explanation: Sacchi demanded a highly compact 25-meter block to choke off passing lanes.

quizQuestions.question: What trap did Sacchi's Milan use to perfection?
quizQuestions.explanation: A highly synchronized backline stepped up in unison to catch attackers offside.

quizQuestions.question: Why was Sacchi's Milan considered revolutionary?
options: They did not use a striker
They dominated with zone-pressing and compactness in an era of man-marking
quizQuestions.explanation: They proved that organized zones could easily defeat individual man-markers.

role-goalkeeper.title: Goalkeeper
role-goalkeeper.description: Traditional shot-stopping, positioning, and goal defense.
role-goalkeeper.introduction: The Goalkeeper is the ultimate defender. Their main job is to prevent the ball from crossing the goal line, utilizing hands inside their box, shot-stopping reflex, and positioning.

sections.heading: Shot-Stopping
sections.content: The core duty. Using reflexes, diving capability, and positioning to block shots and keep clean sheets.

sections.heading: Commanding the Box
sections.content: Catching or punching crosses, communicating with defenders, and organizing the defensive wall during free kicks.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary role of a traditional Goalkeeper?
quizQuestions.explanation: The goalkeeper's main job is goal defense.

quizQuestions.question: Where is the goalkeeper allowed to use their hands?
options: Only inside their own penalty box
quizQuestions.explanation: Goalkeepers can only use their hands inside their own penalty box.

quizQuestions.question: What does 'clean sheet' mean?
options: Conceding zero goals in a match
quizQuestions.explanation: A clean sheet is a match where the team concedes no goals.

quizQuestions.question: How does the goalkeeper organize defenders on free-kicks?
options: By building a wall of players to block the goal angle
quizQuestions.explanation: Organizing a wall blocks the most dangerous angle of the shot.

quizQuestions.question: Which keeper is famous for traditional shot-stopping?
quizQuestions.explanation: Buffon is legendary for his shot-stopping and positioning.

role-sweeper-keeper.title: Sweeper Keeper
role-sweeper-keeper.description: Defending outside the box and launching attacks from deep.
role-sweeper-keeper.introduction: A Sweeper Keeper plays high up, outside their penalty area. They clear long passes behind the high line and participate actively in team passing.

sections.heading: Sweeping Space
sections.content: They sweep the space behind center-backs. If the opponent plays a long ball, the keeper rushes out to clear it before the striker can reach it.

sections.heading: Buildup Link
sections.content: They act as an extra outfield player, comfortable passing under pressure to help beat the press.

quizQuestions.question: What does a Sweeper Keeper do differently?
options: Positions high outside the box to clear long balls
quizQuestions.explanation: They actively sweep the space behind the defense outside their box.

quizQuestions.question: Why is a sweeper keeper vital for high-line systems?
options: They cover the open space behind the high defense
quizQuestions.explanation: A high line leaves space behind, which the keeper must guard by rushing out.

quizQuestions.question: Who is the most famous modern Sweeper Keeper?
quizQuestions.explanation: Manuel Neuer at Bayern and Germany popularized the modern sweeper keeper role.

quizQuestions.question: What skill is highly required for a sweeper keeper?
options: Excellent passing, positioning, and timing when rushing out
quizQuestions.explanation: Composure and timing are critical to avoid cards or open-goal mistakes.

quizQuestions.question: What happens if a sweeper keeper misjudges a ball outside the box?
options: They risk getting bypassed or red-carded for handball
quizQuestions.explanation: Rushing out is high-risk; mistakes lead to open nets or red cards.

role-libero.title: Libero (Tactical Role)
role-libero.description: A free central defender who steps out to launch attacks.
role-libero.introduction: The Libero is a free defender who sits behind the backline. In possession, they carry the ball forward into midfield to playmake.

sections.heading: The Free Man
sections.content: No man-marking duties. The Libero sweeps up loose balls in defense, and acts as an extra midfielder in possession.

sections.heading: Beckenbauer Style
sections.content: Franz Beckenbauer famously defined this role by carrying the ball from deep to orchestrate attacks.

quizQuestions.question: What is the key characteristic of a Libero?
options: They have no man-marking duties and can join the midfield
quizQuestions.explanation: The Libero is a free defender who steps into midfield to playmake.

quizQuestions.question: What is the German term for the Libero?
quizQuestions.explanation: Libero (or Free Defender) is the standard term.

quizQuestions.question: Who is the greatest Libero in football history?
quizQuestions.explanation: Franz 'Der Kaiser' Beckenbauer perfected the Libero role.

quizQuestions.question: Why is the Libero rare in a flat back four?
options: It plays everyone onside, ruining offside traps
quizQuestions.explanation: A deep-lying defender plays attackers onside, so modern lines are kept flat.

quizQuestions.question: How does a modern center-back play like a Libero?
options: By stepping forward into midfield to build play (like John Stones)
quizQuestions.explanation: Ball-playing center-backs stepping into midfield mimics the Libero role.

role-ball-playing-defender.title: Ball Playing Defender
role-ball-playing-defender.description: Center-backs possessing excellent passing range to launch moves.
role-ball-playing-defender.introduction: A Ball Playing Defender is a center-back who is highly comfortable on the ball. They don't just clear it; they play accurate passes to start attacks.

sections.heading: Deep Buildup
sections.content: They act as deep playmakers, picking out line-breaking passes to midfielders or long diagonal switches to wingers.

sections.heading: Press Resistance
sections.content: They remain calm when pressed by opposing strikers, using skill to pass out safely.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary skill of a Ball Playing Defender?
options: Calmness and accurate passing from the back
quizQuestions.explanation: They are valued for their passing range and composure during buildup.

quizQuestions.question: How do they assist the attack?
options: By delivering line-breaking passes to midfielders
quizQuestions.explanation: They start the attack by passing directly through the opponent's front press.

quizQuestions.question: Name a famous Ball Playing Defender.
quizQuestions.explanation: Van Dijk is famous for his calm defense and incredible long diagonal passes.

quizQuestions.question: What is a risk for a ball-playing defender?
options: Overconfidence leading to turnovers near their own goal
quizQuestions.explanation: Trying risky passes at the back can lead to dangerous turnovers.

quizQuestions.question: Why do possession teams value them?
options: They allow the team to build play with control from the goalkeeper
quizQuestions.explanation: Buildup from the back requires defenders comfortable with passing under pressure.

role-stopper.title: Stopper
role-stopper.description: An aggressive center-back who steps up to challenge attackers.
role-stopper.introduction: A Stopper is a physical center-back. They play aggressively, stepping out of the defensive line to challenge forwards and intercept passes before they reach the box.

sections.heading: Interception Focus
sections.content: The Stopper does not wait for the striker to turn. They step up immediately, using strength to win the ball or force the forward backward.

sections.heading: Partnership
sections.content: Often paired with a 'Cover' defender who sits deeper to cover the space left open when the stopper steps up.

quizQuestions.question: What is the main style of a Stopper?
options: Aggressive, stepping out to challenge attackers
quizQuestions.explanation: Stoppers play aggressively to stop attacks before they reach the box.

quizQuestions.question: Who is a Stopper usually paired with?
options: A 'Cover' defender who sits deep to protect the space
quizQuestions.explanation: A cover defender protects the space left open when the stopper steps up.

quizQuestions.question: What physical attribute is key for a Stopper?
quizQuestions.explanation: Winning headers and physical duels requires strength and height.

quizQuestions.question: Name a classic Stopper center-back.
quizQuestions.explanation: Vidić at Man United was a classic aggressive stopper.

quizQuestions.question: What is a risk of a stopper stepping up?
options: Leaving space open behind them if they miss the tackle
quizQuestions.explanation: If the stopper is beaten, the striker has a clear run at the goal.

role-wing-back.title: Wing Back
role-wing-back.description: Wide defenders covering the entire wing in three-back systems.
role-wing-back.introduction: A Wing-Back plays in three-back systems (like 3-5-2). They are responsible for the entire flank, acting as defenders in defense and wingers in attack.

sections.heading: Flank Running
sections.content: They cover the entire wing. In attack, they provide width and cross the ball; in defense, they drop to form a five-man backline.

sections.heading: Stamina Demands
sections.content: The most physically demanding role on the pitch, requiring constant sprinting across 90 minutes.

quizQuestions.question: In which system does a Wing-Back typically play?
quizQuestions.explanation: Wing-backs are the wide outlets in three-back configurations.

quizQuestions.question: What is the main physical requirement for a Wing-Back?
quizQuestions.explanation: Covering the entire flank requires incredible running capacity.

quizQuestions.question: How does the wing-back support the attack?
options: By providing width and crossing from flanks
By staying near their own keeper
quizQuestions.explanation: They act as wingers, crossing and stretching play.

quizQuestions.question: How does the wing-back support the defense?
options: By dropping deep to form a 5-man defense line
By standing in the center circle
quizQuestions.explanation: They drop back to form a temporary five-man backline.

quizQuestions.question: Name a famous attacking Wing-Back.
quizQuestions.explanation: Hakimi and Alexander-Arnold excel at flying wingback runs.

role-inverted-wing-back.title: Inverted Wing Back
role-inverted-wing-back.description: Wing-backs who shift into central midfield during possession.
role-inverted-wing-back.introduction: An Inverted Wing-Back shifts inside to central midfield during possession, acting as a holding midfielder to help control the game and overload the center.

sections.heading: Midfield Shift
sections.content: In possession, they step inside beside the No. 6. This creates a double pivot and frees up advanced midfielders to attack.

sections.heading: Wide Protection
sections.content: When possession is lost, they must rapidly slide back to their defensive fullback position.

quizQuestions.question: Where does an Inverted Wing-Back move in possession?
options: Inside to join the central midfield pivot
quizQuestions.explanation: They step inside to act as midfielders when their team has the ball.

quizQuestions.question: Why do managers use inverted wing-backs?
options: To create central numerical overloads and control possession
quizQuestions.explanation: Adding an extra player to midfield makes it easy to bypass presses.

quizQuestions.question: Which coach famously uses inverted wing-backs?
quizQuestions.explanation: Guardiola has used Lahm, Alaba, Cancelo, and Stones in inverted roles.

quizQuestions.question: What is a main risk of this role?
options: Flanks are exposed to counter-attacks on turnovers
quizQuestions.explanation: Leaving the wing open leaves the team vulnerable to wide counters.

quizQuestions.question: What skill is vital for an inverted wing-back?
options: Composure, passing, and positional awareness under pressure
quizQuestions.explanation: Playing in midfield requires 360-degree awareness and passing skills.

role-full-back.title: Full Back
role-full-back.description: Traditional outside defender focused on wing defense.
role-full-back.introduction: The Fullback is a traditional wide defender. Their primary job is to defend the wings, block crosses, and mark opponent wingers.

sections.heading: Flank Defense
sections.content: Fullbacks sit on the left and right sides of the back four. They must prevent opposing wingers from dribbling past or crossing.

sections.heading: Attacking Support
sections.content: While focused on defense, modern fullbacks are expected to occasionally join attacks, overlapping to cross.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary job of a traditional Fullback?
options: Defend the flanks and mark wingers
quizQuestions.explanation: They are wide defenders focused on protecting the flanks.

quizQuestions.question: Where do fullbacks position themselves in a back four?
options: On the left and right edges of the defensive line
quizQuestions.explanation: They sit on the outer edges of the back four.

quizQuestions.question: What is the fullback's duty when the winger cuts inside?
options: Track them and block the path to the box
quizQuestions.explanation: They must contain the winger's entry toward the center of the pitch.

quizQuestions.question: How does a fullback support the attack?
options: By making overlapping runs to cross
quizQuestions.explanation: They overlap wide areas to provide extra crossing options.

quizQuestions.question: Who is a classic legendary Fullback?
quizQuestions.explanation: Maldini and Neville were legendary defensive fullbacks.

role-defensive-midfielder.title: Defensive Midfielder
role-defensive-midfielder.description: Shielding central defense and sweeping up loose balls.
role-defensive-midfielder.introduction: A Defensive Midfielder (No. 6) sits in front of the defense. They intercept passes, make tackles, and protect the center-backs from direct attacks.

sections.heading: The Shield
sections.content: They block passing lanes to the opponent's strikers, win physical duels in midfield, and recover second balls.

sections.heading: Buildup Role
sections.content: Once they win possession, they play simple, safe passes to the creative playmakers.

quizQuestions.question: What is the main task of a Defensive Midfielder?
options: Shield the defense and disrupt opponent attacks
quizQuestions.explanation: They protect the backline by breaking up play in central areas.

quizQuestions.question: Which shirt number is traditionally associated with this role?
quizQuestions.explanation: The No. 6 is the traditional anchor/defensive midfielder.

quizQuestions.question: What is an interception?
options: Cutting off an opponent's pass to win possession
quizQuestions.explanation: An interception is reading play to block and recover a pass.

quizQuestions.question: Name a famous defensive midfielder.
quizQuestions.explanation: Kante and Makelele are legendary for their workrate and interceptions.

quizQuestions.question: What is the 'Makelele Role' named after?
options: A holding midfielder who protects the defense and plays simple passes
quizQuestions.explanation: Claude Makelele defined the modern holding midfielder role.

role-anchor.title: Anchor
role-anchor.description: A pure holding midfielder who rarely moves from in front of defense.
role-anchor.introduction: An Anchor is a disciplined holding midfielder. They do not join the attack; they stay central, screen the defense, and prioritize positional security.

sections.heading: Stay Home
sections.content: The Anchor's motto is 'stay home'. While other midfielders push forward, the anchor stays in front of the center-backs to block counter-attacks.

sections.heading: Simple Play
sections.content: They win the ball and pass it immediately to nearby playmakers, taking zero risks.

quizQuestions.question: What describes the movement of an Anchor midfielder?
options: Remains stationary in front of the defense to screen passes
quizQuestions.explanation: The anchor sits disciplined in central defense channels.

quizQuestions.question: Does the anchor join the attack?
options: No, they prioritize defensive positioning and security
quizQuestions.explanation: They stay back to protect the defense against transitions.

quizQuestions.question: What is a key quality for an Anchor?
quizQuestions.explanation: Discipline is vital to avoid leaving central spaces unprotected.

quizQuestions.question: Which midfielder type is opposite to the Anchor?
quizQuestions.explanation: A box-to-box midfielder runs the entire pitch, whereas the anchor stays deep.

quizQuestions.question: Give an example of an Anchor player.
quizQuestions.explanation: Mascherano and Casemiro sit deep to block central counters.

role-regista.title: Regista
role-regista.description: A deep playmaker orchestrating patterns from holding midfield.
role-regista.introduction: The Regista is a deep-lying playmaker. Instead of physical defending, they use their vision and long passing range to direct play from holding midfield.

sections.heading: The Conductor
sections.content: They collect the ball from defense and orchestrate the team's attack, switching play with long diagonals.

sections.heading: Defensive Protection
sections.content: They need a physical partner (destroyer) to do the dirty work, leaving them free to create.

quizQuestions.question: What is the main task of a Regista?
options: Dictate play and orchestrate attacks from deep
quizQuestions.explanation: A Regista is a deep-lying conductor of play.

quizQuestions.question: Who is the most famous Regista?
quizQuestions.explanation: Pirlo is the defining modern Regista.

quizQuestions.question: What passing range is expected from a Regista?
quizQuestions.explanation: They must switch play with long, accurate diagonal passes.

quizQuestions.question: Why do they need a defensive partner?
options: To protect them and win back ball possession
quizQuestions.explanation: A physical player (like Gattuso) handles defensive duels, letting the Regista focus on playmaking.

quizQuestions.question: Where is the Regista positioned?
quizQuestions.explanation: They sit deep in midfield to have the best view of the pitch.

role-deep-lying-playmaker.title: Deep-Lying Playmaker
role-deep-lying-playmaker.description: Orchestrating play from deep with dynamic passing range.
role-deep-lying-playmaker.introduction: The Deep-Lying Playmaker sits deep, directing attacks. They use vision and passing to bypass the press and feed forwards.

sections.heading: quarterbacking
sections.content: They act as a deep quarterback, receiving the ball from defenders and passing forward through lines.

sections.heading: Press Resistance
sections.content: They must remain calm under pressure, shielding the ball to find outlets.

quizQuestions.question: What is a Deep-Lying Playmaker?
options: A midfielder sitting deep who orchestrates attacks with long passing
quizQuestions.explanation: They direct attacks from holding midfield zones.

quizQuestions.question: How do they start attacks?
options: By playing accurate long diagonal passes or line-breakers
quizQuestions.explanation: Vision and long passing are their key tools.

quizQuestions.question: Name a classic Deep-Lying Playmaker.
quizQuestions.explanation: Xabi Alonso was legendary for his long-range deep passing.

quizQuestions.question: What is a risk of this role?
options: Turnovers near their own box if pressed intensely
quizQuestions.explanation: Opponents target them to shut down the team's passing engine.

quizQuestions.question: How do they defend?
options: Using positioning to intercept passes and shield the back four
quizQuestions.explanation: They protect the defense with positioning and interceptions.

role-box-to-box.title: Box-to-Box Midfielder
role-box-to-box.description: Running box-to-box to contribute to both defense and attack.
role-box-to-box.introduction: A Box-to-Box Midfielder (No. 8) is a complete player. They run the entire length of the pitch, defending their own box and arriving in the opponent's box to score.

sections.heading: The Engine
sections.content: They must possess elite stamina. They make tackles near their own box, carry the ball forward, and arrive late to finish chances.

sections.heading: Versatility
sections.content: They must be skilled at both winning the ball (tackling) and creating (passing/shooting).

quizQuestions.question: What is the main characteristic of a Box-to-Box midfielder?
options: They run the entire pitch, defending and attacking
quizQuestions.explanation: They cover the entire pitch, from their own box to the opponent's box.

quizQuestions.question: Which shirt number is traditionally associated with this role?
quizQuestions.explanation: The No. 8 is the classic box-to-box midfielder.

quizQuestions.question: What physical attribute is most critical for a box-to-box player?
quizQuestions.explanation: Running the entire pitch for 90 minutes requires incredible cardiovascular stamina.

quizQuestions.question: Name a legendary Box-to-Box midfielder.
quizQuestions.explanation: Gerrard, Keane, Lampard, and Vieira are classic box-to-box giants.

quizQuestions.question: How do they contribute to the attack?
options: Making late runs into the box to score from loose balls
quizQuestions.explanation: Arriving late makes them hard for defenders to mark.

role-mezzala.title: Mezzala
role-mezzala.description: Drifting wide to attack the half-spaces and flanks.
role-mezzala.introduction: The Mezzala is an attacking central midfielder who drifts wide to combine with wingers and exploit the half-spaces.

sections.heading: The Half-Winger
sections.content: They drift from central midfield to the wings, creating passing triangles with the winger and fullback.

sections.heading: Half-Space Attack
sections.content: They run into the gap between the center-back and fullback, creating scoring chances.

quizQuestions.question: What does the Italian word 'Mezzala' mean?
quizQuestions.explanation: Mezzala translates to half-winger.

quizQuestions.question: Where does the Mezzala run?
quizQuestions.explanation: They drift wide into the half-spaces between center and wing.

quizQuestions.question: Which formation suits a Mezzala?
quizQuestions.explanation: Midfield threes (like in 4-3-3) allow the Mezzala to drift wide safely.

quizQuestions.question: How do they help the wingers?
options: Drifting wide to overload the flank (creating 2v1 or 3v2)
quizQuestions.explanation: Their wide runs create numerical overloads on the wing.

quizQuestions.question: Name a modern player with Mezzala qualities.
quizQuestions.explanation: De Bruyne famously drifts wide to cross from the half-spaces.

role-carrilero.title: Carrilero
role-carrilero.description: A lateral midfielder who covers the wings when fullbacks push forward.
role-carrilero.introduction: The Carrilero is a shuttler. They move laterally across the pitch to cover the flanks when fullbacks push forward to attack.

sections.heading: Flank Cover
sections.content: They slide sideways to cover the space left vacant by overlapping fullbacks, keeping the defense secure.

sections.heading: Possession Link
sections.content: They focus on clean, low-risk passing to retain possession.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary movement of a Carrilero?
quizQuestions.explanation: They shuttle laterally to protect wide spaces.

quizQuestions.question: Why are they useful in diamond formations?
options: They cover the empty flanks when fullbacks overlap
quizQuestions.explanation: Diamond formations lack wingers, so Carrileros cover the flanks.

quizQuestions.question: Do Carrileros focus on scoring?
options: No, they prioritize defensive cover and possession
quizQuestions.explanation: Their role is defensive balance and possession, not scoring.

quizQuestions.question: What is the English term for Carrilero?
quizQuestions.explanation: Carrilero translates to shuttler.

quizQuestions.question: How do they assist the buildup?
options: Providing safe passing outlets on the sides of midfield
quizQuestions.explanation: They offer simple lateral passing options to maintain possession.

role-attacking-midfielder.title: Attacking Midfielder
role-attacking-midfielder.description: The creative link playing behind strikers to generate chances.
role-attacking-midfielder.introduction: The Attacking Midfielder (No. 10) sits behind the strikers. They use vision, passing, and dribbling to create scoring chances and score goals.

sections.heading: The Playmaker
sections.content: They play in the pocket between the opponent's midfield and defense, unlocking lines with through balls.

sections.heading: Goal Threat
sections.content: They also score goals, shooting from the edge of the box or making late runs.

quizQuestions.question: What is the main task of an Attacking Midfielder?
options: Create scoring chances and link midfield to attack
quizQuestions.explanation: They are the team's main creative link in the final third.

quizQuestions.question: Which shirt number is traditionally associated with this role?
quizQuestions.explanation: The No. 10 is the traditional attacking playmaker.

quizQuestions.question: Where do they position themselves?
options: In the pocket between the opponent's midfield and defense
quizQuestions.explanation: They sit 'in the hole' to have space to create.

quizQuestions.question: What pass is their signature weapon?
options: A line-breaking through ball into the box
quizQuestions.explanation: Through balls split defenders, releasing strikers.

quizQuestions.question: Name a famous modern Attacking Midfielder.
quizQuestions.explanation: De Bruyne and Fernandes are elite attacking creators.

role-trequartista.title: Trequartista
role-trequartista.description: A final third playmaker free of defensive duties.
role-trequartista.introduction: The Trequartista is a creative genius who operates in the final third. They focus entirely on creativity, exempted from defensive work.

sections.heading: Pure Creativity
sections.content: They drift between midfield and attack, using skills and through balls to feed forwards.

sections.heading: Defensive Exemption
sections.content: Preserving their energy ensures they are sharp and lethal on counter-attacks.

quizQuestions.question: What does 'Trequartista' mean?
quizQuestions.explanation: It refers to their positioning in the three-quarter zone of the pitch.

quizQuestions.question: What is a key benefit of freeing them from defense?
options: They are fresh and available on transitions
quizQuestions.explanation: Preserving energy keeps them sharp to launch counters.

quizQuestions.question: Name a famous Italian Trequartista.
quizQuestions.explanation: Totti was the ultimate Roma Trequartista.

quizQuestions.question: Where does the Trequartista play?
options: In the pocket behind the strikers
quizQuestions.explanation: They drift in the hole behind the forwards.

quizQuestions.question: What happens if they are marked closely?
options: They drift wide or drop deep to pull markers out of position
quizQuestions.explanation: Roaming helps them escape close markers.

role-enganche.title: Enganche
role-enganche.description: A stationary central playmaker linking midfield to attack.
role-enganche.introduction: The Enganche is a traditional stationary playmaker. They stay in the center, acting as the pivot hook to distribute passes.

sections.heading: The Hook
sections.content: They stay central, acting as the link. They do not run the channels, using passing to move the team.

sections.heading: Modern Scarcity
sections.content: High-tempo modern pressing has made the slow, stationary Enganche rare.

quizQuestions.question: What does 'Enganche' mean in Spanish?
quizQuestions.explanation: Enganche translates to hook.

quizQuestions.question: What is the movement of a classic Enganche?
quizQuestions.explanation: They stand in the center, letting their passing do the work.

quizQuestions.question: Who is a famous example of this role?
quizQuestions.explanation: Riquelme is the classic South American Enganche.

quizQuestions.question: Why is the Enganche rare today?
options: Modern pressing requires all players to defend and run
quizQuestions.explanation: Modern teams cannot afford a passenger who does not defend.

quizQuestions.question: What is their primary skill?
quizQuestions.explanation: They excel at unlocking defenses with passes.

role-winger.title: Winger
role-winger.description: Traditional wide attacker crossing the ball from near touchlines.
role-winger.introduction: A Winger plays on the flanks. They hug the touchline, beat fullbacks with speed and dribbling, and cross the ball into the box.

sections.heading: Hugging the Touchline
sections.content: They stay wide, stretching the defense and creating 1v1 duels against the fullback.

sections.heading: Crossing
sections.content: They run down the flank to cross with their natural foot into the box.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary job of a traditional Winger?
options: Stay wide, beat fullbacks, and cross
quizQuestions.explanation: Traditional wingers hug the line to cross.

quizQuestions.question: What foot does a right-winger use to cross?
quizQuestions.explanation: A right-winger uses their right foot for direct crosses.

quizQuestions.question: What is the benefit of staying wide?
options: Stretches the defense, opening gaps in the center
quizQuestions.explanation: Stretching the backline creates central spaces.

quizQuestions.question: Who is a classic traditional Winger?
quizQuestions.explanation: Beckham and Giggs are classic touchline crossers.

quizQuestions.question: What is a winger's main duel?
quizQuestions.explanation: They battle the fullback to reach the crossing zone.

role-inverted-winger.title: Inverted Winger
role-inverted-winger.description: Wide attacker cutting inside on opposite foot to shoot.
role-inverted-winger.introduction: An Inverted Winger plays on the opposite wing of their dominant foot. They cut inside onto their strong foot to shoot or create.

sections.heading: Cutting Inside
sections.content: They cut diagonally from wide, opening up direct shooting angles on their strong foot.

sections.heading: Fullback Space
sections.content: Drifting inside clears the wing corridor for overlapping fullbacks to cross.

quizQuestions.question: What is an Inverted Winger?
options: Winger playing on opposite side of their strong foot
quizQuestions.explanation: They play on the opposite flank of their strong foot.

quizQuestions.question: What is their primary attacking move?
options: Cutting inside to shoot or pass
quizQuestions.explanation: They cut inside to shoot or create.

quizQuestions.question: Who is a famous Inverted Winger?
quizQuestions.explanation: Robben cutting inside from the right was his signature move.

quizQuestions.question: What space is opened when they cut inside?
options: The wing corridor for overlapping fullbacks
quizQuestions.explanation: Their inside movement clears the flank for the fullback.

quizQuestions.question: What threat do they offer?
options: Direct goal scoring threats from central angles
quizQuestions.explanation: They act as extra forwards by shooting from central areas.

role-inside-forward.title: Inside Forward
role-inside-forward.description: Wingers who play very high and act like second strikers.
role-inside-forward.introduction: An Inside Forward starts wide but plays very high, cutting inside to act as a second striker in the box rather than a playmaker.

sections.heading: Goalscoring Focus
sections.content: They starting wide but their main target is the goal. They cut inside to finish chances, leaving width to fullbacks.

sections.heading: Salah Style
sections.content: Mohamed Salah at Liverpool is a classic example, starting wide but scoring like a central forward.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary goal of an Inside Forward?
options: Cut inside and enter the box to act as a scorer
quizQuestions.explanation: They cut inside to act as second strikers in the box.

quizQuestions.question: How do they differ from inverted wingers?
options: They play higher, focusing on scoring inside the box
quizQuestions.explanation: Inside forwards are high goal-scorers who act like strikers, whereas inverted wingers can be creators.

quizQuestions.question: Name a modern player who plays as an Inside Forward.
quizQuestions.explanation: Salah starts wide but cuts inside to score high numbers of goals.

quizQuestions.question: Who provides the width in an inside forward system?
quizQuestions.explanation: Fullbacks overlap to provide width as forwards cut inside.

quizQuestions.question: What is their run path?
options: Diagonal runs from wide into the penalty area
quizQuestions.explanation: They make diagonal runs from the wings directly into the box.

role-shadow-striker.title: Shadow Striker
role-shadow-striker.description: Second striker arriving late in the box to convert flick-ons.
role-shadow-striker.introduction: A Shadow Striker plays behind the forward. They use the forward's physical battles as a screen, arriving late in the box to finish loose balls.

sections.heading: Late Runs
sections.content: They wait for the main striker to engage center-backs, then sprint past them to finish.

sections.heading: Anticipation
sections.content: They excel at reading where knockdowns will land, arriving unmarked.

quizQuestions.question: Where does the Shadow Striker start their run?
options: Deep in midfield, arriving late in the box
quizQuestions.explanation: They start deep, making late runs into the box.

quizQuestions.question: Who do they play off of?
options: A physical target striker who screens center-backs
quizQuestions.explanation: They exploit spaces created by a physical central forward.

quizQuestions.question: Why are they hard to mark?
options: Their runs are late and start from deep midfield
quizQuestions.explanation: Defenders are busy with the striker, failing to track the late run.

quizQuestions.question: Name a player famous for this style.
quizQuestions.explanation: Müller is famous for late, ghosting box runs.

quizQuestions.question: What is their primary duty?
quizQuestions.explanation: They are goalscoring playmakers who finish box chances.

role-false-9.title: False 9
role-false-9.description: A forward dropping into midfield to confuse center-backs.
role-false-9.introduction: The False 9 is a striker who drops deep. This movement pulls defenders out of shape and opens space for wide runs.

sections.heading: The Trap
sections.content: By dropping deep, they force center-backs to make a decision: follow them or stay back.

sections.heading: Wide Cuts
sections.content: Wingers cut inside to attack the space the False 9 vacated.

quizQuestions.question: What is the main movement of a False 9?
options: Drop deep into midfield to draw defenders
quizQuestions.explanation: The False 9 drops deep to playmake and disrupt center-backs.

quizQuestions.question: Who famously played this under Pep at Barca?
quizQuestions.explanation: Messi revolutionized the False 9 role under Guardiola.

quizQuestions.question: Who runs into the empty space?
quizQuestions.explanation: Wingers exploit the space behind the defense.

quizQuestions.question: What does this create in midfield?
quizQuestions.explanation: Dropping deep gives the team an extra midfielder.

quizQuestions.question: What is the center-back dilemma?
options: Follow the dropping striker or stay in position
quizQuestions.explanation: Following opens space; staying back gives the playmaker time.

role-target-man.title: Target Man
role-target-man.description: A tall striker who holds up play and wins aerial battles.
role-target-man.introduction: A Target Man is a physical striker. They receive direct long passes, shield the ball, and link up with runners.

sections.heading: Hold Up Play
sections.content: They use their body to keep defenders away, allowing midfielders time to join the attack.

sections.heading: Aerial Target
sections.content: They win long balls, flicking them on to fast wingers.

quizQuestions.question: What is the main skill of a Target Man?
options: Physical hold-up play and aerial dominance
quizQuestions.explanation: They use strength to hold the ball and win headers.

quizQuestions.question: What physical attribute is vital?
quizQuestions.explanation: Strength and height are needed to battle center-backs.

quizQuestions.question: What is a flick-on?
options: A header guiding the ball to runners behind defense
quizQuestions.explanation: Flick-ons guide long balls directly to fast teammates.

quizQuestions.question: Give an example of a Target Man.
quizQuestions.explanation: Ibrahimović and Drogba are classic physical target strikers.

quizQuestions.question: Who should play close to the target man?
options: Fast wingers or a running midfielder
quizQuestions.explanation: They need runners nearby to collect their knockdowns.

role-poacher.title: Poacher
role-poacher.description: A clinical box striker who scores from close range.
role-poacher.introduction: A Poacher is a penalty-box striker. They do not participate in buildup or defend; they focus entirely on finding space in the box to finish chances.

sections.heading: Penalty Box Mastery
sections.content: They live in the penalty box. They have elite anticipation, reacting first to deflections or low crosses to tap the ball in.

sections.heading: Off-the-ball Sprints
sections.content: They make short, sharp sprints to beat their marker to the ball in high-danger zones.

quizQuestions.question: Where does a Poacher spend most of the match?
quizQuestions.explanation: Poachers operate almost exclusively inside the penalty box.

quizQuestions.question: Do poachers participate heavily in buildup play?
options: No, they focus entirely on positioning and finishing in the box
quizQuestions.explanation: Poachers stay high, letting others create so they can focus on scoring.

quizQuestions.question: What is their key strength?
options: Clinical finishing and reaction speed in the box
quizQuestions.explanation: Anticipation and one-touch finishing are their main weapons.

quizQuestions.question: Which legendary player is a classic Poacher?
quizQuestions.explanation: Inzaghi was famous for living on the offside line and scoring tap-ins.

quizQuestions.question: How do they score most of their goals?
quizQuestions.explanation: They specialize in close-range finishes and rebounds.

role-pressing-forward.title: Pressing Forward
role-pressing-forward.description: Striker whose main job is to trigger the high press.
role-pressing-forward.introduction: A Pressing Forward leads the defense from the front. They sprint to close down opponent center-backs and the goalkeeper, forcing errors and blocking passing lanes.

sections.heading: Defending from the Front
sections.content: Their main job is to disrupt the opponent's buildup. They sprint to pressure center-backs, forcing them to make quick decisions or clear the ball long.

sections.heading: Stamina Demands
sections.content: Requires immense stamina and tactical intelligence to know when to press and how to block passing channels.

quizQuestions.question: What is the main task of a Pressing Forward?
options: Stay in the box and wait for crosses
Sprint to press opponent defenders and goalkeeper
quizQuestions.explanation: They lead the high press, closing down the opponent's backline.

quizQuestions.question: What physical attribute is most vital for this role?
quizQuestions.explanation: Chasing defenders all game requires incredible physical workrate.

quizQuestions.question: Who is a famous modern Pressing Forward?
quizQuestions.explanation: Firmino at Liverpool was the key defensive forward who triggered Klopp's press.

quizQuestions.question: What does their press force center-backs to do?
options: Make mistakes or clear the ball long under pressure
quizQuestions.explanation: Pressure forces errors and rushed clearances.

quizQuestions.question: Do pressing forwards also score?
options: Yes, they score from winning the ball high up in transition
quizQuestions.explanation: Winning turnovers near the box leads to easy goals.

role-complete-forward.title: Complete Forward
role-complete-forward.description: Possessing stats to hold up, create, score, and press.
role-complete-forward.introduction: The Complete Forward possesses all attacking qualities. They can hold up play, run in behind, create chances, score headers, and press defenders — a universal striker.

sections.heading: The Universal Striker
sections.content: They have no weaknesses. They can play as a target man, a poacher, or drop deep like a False 9, adapting to what the match requires.

sections.heading: Tactical Value
sections.content: Extremely rare and valuable, as they allow the coach to change styles mid-match without making substitutions.

quizQuestions.question: What defines a Complete Forward?
options: They possess all attacking skills — hold-up, speed, creation, and finishing
quizQuestions.explanation: A complete forward has no weaknesses, combining all forward roles.

quizQuestions.question: Why are complete forwards highly valued?
options: They allow the team to adapt to any style of play
quizQuestions.explanation: They can hold play, run behind, or drop deep, adjusting to matches.

quizQuestions.question: Name a modern Complete Forward.
quizQuestions.explanation: Kane and Lewandowski are elite at scoring, holding up play, and linking with midfield.

quizQuestions.question: What is their goal threat level?
options: Elite, scoring from headers, long shots, and box tap-ins
quizQuestions.explanation: They can finish from any angle and with any technique.

quizQuestions.question: What is their defensive contribution?
options: Active, pressing defenders and winning headers on corners
quizQuestions.explanation: They contribute to defense by pressing from the front and helping on set pieces.
